title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Integrals (Indefinite)
description: Integration as antiderivative, standard integrals, substitution method
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The integral ∫xⁿ dx = ? (n ≠ −1)
questions.explanation: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C (Power Rule for integration). This is the reverse of d/dx(xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)) = xⁿ. '+C' is the constant of integration (representing all antiderivatives).

questions.question: ∫cos x dx = ?
questions.explanation: ∫cos x dx = sin x + C. Verify: d/dx(sin x) = cos x. ✓ Other standard integrals: ∫sin x dx = −cos x + C; ∫sec²x dx = tan x + C.

questions.question: ∫eˣ dx = ?
questions.explanation: ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C. The exponential function is its own derivative AND its own antiderivative (unique property). ∫aˣ dx = aˣ/ln a + C (for constant a > 0, a ≠ 1).

questions.question: ∫1/x dx = ? (x ≠ 0)
questions.explanation: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C. This is the special case of the power rule (n = −1), which is excluded from ∫xⁿdx formula. Verify: d/dx(ln|x|) = 1/x. ✓

questions.question: Evaluate: ∫(3x² + 2x + 1) dx
questions.explanation: ∫(3x²+2x+1)dx = 3x³/3 + 2x²/2 + x + C = x³ + x² + x + C. Each term integrated separately.

questions.question: Substitution method: ∫f(g(x))g'(x) dx. Let u = g(x), then the integral becomes:
questions.explanation: Substitution (u-substitution): let u = g(x), du = g'(x)dx. Then ∫f(g(x))g'(x)dx = ∫f(u)du. Simplifies the integral to a standard form.

questions.question: Evaluate: ∫2x(x² + 1)⁵ dx
questions.explanation: Let u = x²+1, du = 2x dx. ∫u⁵ du = u⁶/6 + C = (x²+1)⁶/6 + C.

questions.question: ∫sec²x dx = ?
questions.explanation: ∫sec²x dx = tan x + C. Verify: d/dx(tan x) = sec²x. ✓ Other results: ∫sec x tan x dx = sec x + C; ∫cosec²x dx = −cot x + C.

questions.question: ∫dx/(1 + x²) = ?
questions.explanation: ∫dx/(1+x²) = tan⁻¹x + C. This is the integral leading to the arctan (inverse tangent) function. Similarly: ∫dx/√(1−x²) = sin⁻¹x + C.

questions.question: Integration by parts formula: ∫u dv = ?
questions.explanation: Integration by Parts: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du. Choose u as the function that simplifies on differentiation (ILATE: Inverse trig, Logarithm, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫x eˣ dx using integration by parts.
questions.explanation: Let u = x (→ du = dx), dv = eˣ dx (→ v = eˣ). ∫x eˣ dx = x eˣ − ∫eˣ dx = x eˣ − eˣ + C = eˣ(x−1) + C.

questions.question: ∫sin x dx = ?
questions.explanation: ∫sin x dx = −cos x + C. Verify: d/dx(−cos x) = sin x. ✓

questions.question: Evaluate: ∫(2x + 3)/(x² + 3x + 5) dx
questions.explanation: Notice the numerator (2x+3) is the derivative of the denominator (x²+3x+5). So ∫f'(x)/f(x) dx = ln|f(x)| + C. → ln|x²+3x+5| + C.

questions.question: ∫dx/√(1−x²) = ?
questions.explanation: ∫dx/√(1−x²) = sin⁻¹x + C. This is the integral definition of arcsin. Domain: −1 < x < 1.

questions.question: The constant of integration C in ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C represents:
options: The fact that there are infinitely many antiderivatives (differing by a constant)
questions.explanation: Any constant C satisfies d/dx(F(x)+C) = f(x). So there are infinitely many antiderivatives, all differing by a constant. To find a specific one, you need an initial condition (boundary condition).
